title_en: Chapter 4: The Echo Beyond The Veil
title_vi: Chương 4: Tiếng Vọng Sau Tấm Màn
content_en:
The light around the cut withdrew another fraction.

Not quickly. Not in panic. It receded from the fine line in the Veil like water drawing back from a sheet of newly heated metal, leaving behind a transparent interval that no longer reflected anything standing before it.

Michael was already between that interval and the stair.

He did not draw his sword. His hand merely rested on the hilt, yet the weight gathered around his armor pressed into the stone, dimming the engraved paths one ring at a time. Gabriel lowered his staff. A seal closed above the stairway, barring everyone on the upper level from descending farther.

“No one touches it,” Raphael said.

Healiangel looked at his fingertip.

The vibration that had passed through him was still there. It did not hurt. A wound hurt because what had been divided remembered that its parts once belonged together. The thing on the Veil held no such memory. Its two edges lay parallel and flawless, so clean that not a single filament of light remained caught between them.

Lucifer stood close beside him. “You said this was not a crack.”

“It is not.”

“Then something made it.”

Michael turned. “Nothing yet permits that conclusion.”

Lucifer indicated the line with a tilt of his chin. “Does light cut itself into a perfect line?”

“I said we have no conclusion.”

“And while you wait for a word safe enough to use, it is opening.”

The cut widened by the thickness of a feather barb.

No darkness spilled from within. What appeared was only an absence of depth. Healiangel looked into it and could not tell where his sight came to rest. A moment later he realized that the sound of the golden river above had vanished from his left ear, though his right could still hear it clearly.

He shifted his head.

The sound returned.

“It takes away direction,” he said.

Raphael approached and stopped beyond arm’s reach. “Explain.”

“When I look straight at it, I can no longer tell where the river is. It does not silence the sound. It severs the bond between the sound and the place that made it.”

Gabriel raised his staff. The characters around the seal began to turn.

“Everyone step back from the boundary.”

Michael did not move.

“You as well,” Gabriel said.

“If it breaches the Veil, I need to be here.”

“If it reacts to those who just crossed, your presence may be what drives it through.”

Michael watched the cut. His hand left the sword before he took one step back.

Lucifer remained where he was.

Gabriel turned to him.

“I carry no sword,” Lucifer said.

“You do not need one to be the greatest force in this chamber.”

Light rose along Lucifer’s wings. Healiangel expected an answer. Instead, Lucifer looked at Michael’s hand, newly removed from the hilt, then retreated with him to the outer ring of inscriptions.

Raphael knelt before the Veil.

He did not touch the cut. He placed both hands on the stone floor, one on either side of it. White light left his wrists, ran outward in a thin circle, and stopped precisely one finger-joint from the line. Where the light ended, the surface of the Veil sank inward by the slightest measure.

The cut did not change.

Raphael increased the pressure of his power. The characters on the metal band wound around his wrist flared. Adam’s and Lilith’s two life-rhythms appeared, faster now that they were awake, but still steady. The healing light continued to press forward.

The depression around the cut deepened.

The line remained still, refusing to bend with the surface under strain.

Raphael withdrew his hands.

“It does not belong to the structure I am touching.”

Lucifer looked at him. “In other words?”

“I can deform the Veil around it. I cannot make it deform with the Veil.”

“An object lodged inside the wound?” Michael asked.

“No sign of life. No matter. No light.” Raphael rose. “I do not know what to call it.”

A very small sound occurred.

No one heard it with the ear. It appeared, one after another, in the wing-bones of the four who had crossed the Veil, like a fingernail tapping on four different doors.

Michael received it first. The plates over his shoulders locked tight.

Raphael next. The metal band at his wrist flashed white.

Healiangel felt the tapping pass through his mark and spread so widely that every feather lifted.

Lucifer was last.

The cut shone as a hair-thin thread of gold, then went dark.

It had just returned the marks of all four.

Not intact. Michael’s mark had lost its weight. Raphael’s no longer held the two life-rhythms. Lucifer’s retained heat but no light. Healiangel’s had been replayed in reverse, contracting from its widest reach toward a single point.

He stepped back.

Lucifer caught his arm before his heel struck the stair.

“What did it do to you?”

“Nothing.” Healiangel heard his own voice turn dry. “It tried again the way each of us touched it.”

“Tried?” Michael asked.

Healiangel looked at the cut, now dark once more.

“Like an echo,” he said. “But this echo does not return sound. It returns structure.”

Gabriel turned his staff.

Seven layers of sealing descended around the Veil at once. The first passed over the cut without changing shape. The second did the same. When the third reached the line, the characters touching its edge were split cleanly in two. Both halves remained lit. They continued moving in opposite directions, no longer aware that they had once belonged to the same word.

Gabriel stilled the staff.

“Summon Uriel.”

✦

Uriel arrived before the third layer of sealing had fully gone dark.

Amber light descended the stair ahead of him.

It swept beneath the stone arches, revealing ancient channels of script beneath Heaven’s white radiance. When Uriel crossed the ward, the deep-gold wings behind him remained half-open. Each tier of feathers carried a different color at the edge: heated copper, burning honey, the gold of metal just drawn from flame. Yet no heat came with them. The air around him merely became dry and exact, as though every invisible mote of dust had been compelled to stand in its proper place.

Uriel looked at the five who waited, then at the Veil.

“Who touched it first?”

“I did,” Healiangel said.

“Before or after it opened?”

“After.”

“How many times did it respond to you?”

“Twice. The first was a vibration. The second time it replayed the marks of all four who had crossed.”

Uriel nodded and asked nothing more.

He stepped into the inscribed ring Raphael had vacated. His wings opened fully. Amber light spread across the Veil in parallel lines, not piercing the surface but gliding along it. As each line approached the cut, it divided and slipped to either side.

Uriel changed the angle of his wings.

The light advanced again. This time it arced over the cut and converged at a point beneath it. The Veil appeared as layers of transparency laid one over another: the nearest trembled with the golden river; a deeper layer bowed beneath Earth’s gravity; the last could be seen only when the amber light crossed them and broke into short, displaced strokes.

The cut passed straight through them all.

Not one layer held its edge.

“The Veil did not open this path,” Uriel said.

Lucifer moved closer to the ring of light. “Then it came from the other side.”

“It did not begin on ours.”

“What difference is there between those statements?”

Uriel looked at him. “Mine says only what the light proves.”

Lucifer was silent for a moment. “I begin to understand why Gabriel summoned you.”

“Gabriel summoned me because all of you stood around an unknown line and gave it enough marks to repeat.”

Michael intervened before the light on Lucifer’s wings could change. “Can it be closed?”

Uriel turned back to the Veil. “Not from this side.”

“From Earth?” Raphael asked.

“If the cut crosses every layer, there must be a corresponding edge below. It may be bearing force. It may not.”

Gabriel looked at the metal band around Raphael’s wrist. “The two humans?”

“Still stable.”

“Are they near the opposite point?”

Raphael closed his eyes. Two rows of characters flowed around his wrist. “Not near enough for me to determine. The Veil is misdirecting perception.”

Michael drew his sword. He laid the silver blade flat across the floor, its point aimed at a passage-mark three inscribed rings from the cut.

“Open another way.”

Gabriel did not lower the staff.

“If the cut is gathering the marks of those who cross, opening another passage may give it exactly what it needs.”

“So we leave an unknown line suspended between two realms?” Lucifer asked.

“I did not say we leave it.”

“You are searching for a way to act that leaves no one responsible if it fails.”

Gabriel turned to him. “And you are searching for an answer large enough to justify keeping it open.”

The air between them tightened.

Healiangel continued to study the layers Uriel had revealed. The cut ran through all of them, yet in the deepest layer there was a change so slight it was almost nothing. Each time the two life-rhythms at Raphael’s wrist rose together, the amber line there leaned to one side.

“There is a connection to Earth,” he said.

Raphael came beside him. “Are you certain?”

“Not to the two of them. To the gravity below.” Healiangel pointed to the deepest layer. “The far edge is under strain. If this continues, we will no longer be able to choose where it opens.”

Uriel followed his finger. He changed the angle of his wings once more. The deepest amber line shuddered, and a dark trace ran along it toward Earth.

“Healiangel is right.”

Gabriel lowered his staff.

“Who goes?”

“I do,” Michael said.

“As do I,” Healiangel said.

Uriel folded his wings partway. “I need to see the lower edge.”

Three gazes turned toward Lucifer.

He gave a quiet laugh. “You are deciding whether it is safer to keep me beside a cut or leave me alone with the rest of Heaven.”

Michael sheathed his sword. “You come.”

Gabriel looked at him.

“If it repeats our marks,” Michael said, “I want to see what it does with the strongest one.”

“A beautiful reason,” Lucifer replied, “for calling suspicion necessity.”

“Would you rather remain?”

Lucifer looked at the Veil. “No.”

Raphael removed the metal band from his wrist and wound it around Healiangel’s. Adam’s and Lilith’s two life-rhythms continued beneath the white metal.

“I will remain on this side,” he said. “If their rhythms change, you will know before you see it.”

Healiangel nodded.

Raphael did not release his wrist.

“To hear one realm is burden enough,” he said quietly. “If whatever lies behind this forces you to hear both, do not carry them inside yourself.”

“And if there is nowhere else to hold them?”

“Then call us.”

Healiangel looked at Raphael’s hand on his wrist. In the healing chambers, Raphael always knew the exact moment to support a being and the exact moment to let it bear its own weight. This time, his fingers remained longer than they usually did.

“I will call,” Healiangel said.

Gabriel opened the passage.

The Veil divided at the third inscribed ring. Michael crossed first. Healiangel followed, then Lucifer. Uriel came last, his amber wings drawn close so their light would not touch the cut several paces away.

The passage closed after three beats.

The cut lit on the fourth.

✦

Earth received them with the smell of rising water.

Rain had fallen upstream. The river beyond the garden had turned reddish brown, carrying branches, rotted leaves, and patches of white foam. It had not yet broken its banks, but the ground beneath the grass had softened. Each step of the four angels left a hollow that slowly filled with water.

Uriel opened his wings the moment he touched the ground.

Amber light swept low among the trees. The shadows of the leaves stretched in one direction, except for the shadow of a tree burned in an age long past. Its black trunk leaned above the high bank outside Eden, nearly hidden beneath climbing vines. Under Uriel’s light, its shadow divided into two halves.

Between them ran a line with no color.

“There,” Uriel said.

Michael moved toward the tree. Before his third step, Lucifer caught his shoulder and pulled him back.

The earth directly before Michael’s boot slid away from the bank.

A shield-wide sheet of grass dropped into the river. The current carried it off, but the sound of the fall arrived late. In that delayed interval, the colorless line in the tree’s shadow trembled once.

Michael looked at Lucifer’s hand, still resting on his shoulder.

Lucifer released him. “You may thank me later.”

“I was about to.”

Lucifer regarded him as if uncertain whether the answer had been mockery. Michael had already turned back toward the riverbank.

The metal band around Healiangel’s wrist grew hot.

The two life-rhythms quickened.

He looked toward the garden.

Adam and Lilith stood on opposite sides of a narrow branch of water newly split from the main river. The morning before, it had been no more than a dry channel. Rain had filled it into a swift knee-deep current. On the nearer bank, Adam had placed three flat stones to form a crossing. He held a fourth. Across from him, Lilith stood with a bundle of long branches against her chest.

She pointed to the water, then to the sky.

“Water,” Adam said.

Lilith shook her head. With one branch she drew a winding line through the mud, from upstream to their feet, then spread her fingers wide.

Adam studied the drawing. “Water... comes.”

She nodded, then pointed to the three stones already sinking.

Adam set down the fourth.

Lilith did not cross.

He struck the stone with his palm, then held out his hand to her.

She looked at the offered hand. One corner of her mouth lifted. Then she lowered the bundle, chose the longest branch, and laid it across the current above the stones.

“No,” Adam said.

Lilith tested it with one foot.

The wood bowed but did not break.

Adam pointed to his path of stones. Lilith pointed to her branch. They repeated their gestures, faster each time, as though an intention might become true simply by being stated again.

Lucifer watched them from among the trees. “They found a way to disagree before they had enough words.”

“Words merely make some disagreements harder to conceal,” Uriel said.

Lilith gathered the remaining branches and stepped onto the trunk.

Adam dropped the stone and lunged to hold the end on his side. She took two steps. The current struck her legs, pressing the leaves wrapped around her body against her skin. The trunk slipped through the mud.

Adam forced it down.

Lilith continued.

The colorless line in the burned tree’s shadow trembled a second time.

Direction vanished from the air around the bank.

Wind still moved through the canopy, but the water beneath it suddenly went flat. Insects fell silent on one side. Adam raised his head as though he had heard an absence for which he had no name.

The earth beneath his hands collapsed.

The end of the trunk tore free.

Lilith fell.

Michael opened his wings.

Lucifer had already moved half a step before him.

“Wait,” Healiangel said.

Lilith managed to lock one arm around the trunk. The bundle of branches was torn from her chest and caught in the roots below. Her shoulder struck the bank, forcing the breath from her. The current swung her body sideways.

Adam lay flat at the edge. He reached with both hands, but the distance was still too great.

“Lilith.”

She looked up.

Adam slid farther. Earth broke away beneath his chest. He caught her wrist at the moment the root she held tore loose from the bank.

Their hands locked.

Her weight dragged half of Adam’s body over the edge.

Michael kept his wings spread. Silver feathers trembled in the directionless wind. With a single movement, he could have pinned the whole riverbank in place.

Lucifer looked at him. “If you do it, they will never know.”

“I know.”

“Then what is holding you back?”

Michael did not answer.

Below them, Lilith did not try to climb straight upward. She saw Adam’s feet slipping, saw the trunk floating diagonally across the current, and twisted her body. One foot found purchase on the wood. She pushed down.

Adam was pulled forward, but his wrist no longer bore all of her weight. He planted an elbow in the mud and gained a little ground.

Lilith pushed again.

The trunk wedged between two stones.

She rose high enough to throw her other arm over the bank. Adam caught her at the elbow and pulled. Lilith dragged herself free of the water and fell across him. For a moment they lay still, gasping.

A crack sounded beneath the edge.

The rest of the bank gave way.

Adam shoved Lilith inward. He could not free his leg in time. The collapsing earth swept one side of his body into the current. Lilith turned the instant she regained her feet.

She dropped into the same place Adam had occupied, but did not seize the hand flailing toward her. Instead, she slid both arms beneath his, locked her own wrists, and threw all her weight backward.

Adam kicked against the wall of mud.

Once.

Twice.

On the third attempt, he slid over the edge. Lilith was pulled down with him. They rolled across the grass until a great root stopped them.

Neither rose at once.

Adam sat up first, mud covering half his face. He looked at the current that had swallowed his path of stones, then at Lilith’s trunk still lodged between the rocks.

Lilith looked as well.

A sound broke from her throat.

Adam startled. Then he recognized it as the sound they had made when they fell together on their first morning.

He repeated it.

Their laughter was still rough, brief, and tangled with breath, yet it crossed the river more easily than any name they had made.

Adam stood. His left leg buckled.

Lilith offered her hand.

He took it. When Adam pulled, Lilith was drawn forward; she braced one foot, he shifted his weight, and together they rose in a clumsy movement that belonged to neither of them alone.

No hand remained above the other long enough to make the other person merely the one who had been saved.

Healiangel felt the two life-rhythms at his wrist begin to slow.

Michael folded his wings.

Lucifer continued watching the two mud-covered humans. “They did not wait for us to guide them.”

“No,” Michael said.

Lucifer turned, perhaps expecting a rebuttal.

Michael watched Adam retrieve the branches caught in the roots while Lilith reset the trunk across the current.

“Nor do they need to be helpless in order to deserve protection,” he said.

Something shifted, almost imperceptibly, in Lucifer’s expression.

He turned away before Michael could see it clearly.

From beside the burned tree, Uriel called, “It is opening again.”

✦

The lower edge of the cut lay in shadow, but did not belong to shadow.

Uriel had stripped every trace of light from the trunk. Sunlight passed through the spaces between the branches; amber radiance from his wings covered the ground; Lucifer held a golden glow over the river. Even so, the line remained colorless. It began at a root raised from the earth, ran up the burned trunk, and ended in open air, as long as an angel’s arm.

Michael drove his sword into the ground to the north. Weight flowed through the silver blade and held the bank against further collapse.

Uriel stood to the south, his wings spread at a narrow angle. Amber lines marked each layer of the Veil, though from Earth no one could see its surface.

Lucifer held the west.

Healiangel stepped into the remaining space.

“It took our marks above,” Michael said. “Do not give it more.”

“To know what it holds, I have to touch it.”

“You already did.”

“With one fingertip. I heard only the outer edge.”

Lucifer looked at the cut. “Let him.”

Michael did not turn. “You do not know what it will take.”

“Neither do you.”

“That is why I said stop.”

“That is what you call every boundary you are afraid to cross.”

The silver blade sank deeper into the earth.

“And you call every boundary a prison,” Michael replied, “so you never have to admit that what lies beyond it may not belong to you.”

The golden light in the west flared. The river became a long band of brightness.

“Enough,” Healiangel said.

Both of them looked at him.

“Do not make me heal one cut while the two of you open another.”

Lucifer lowered his hand. The light over the river softened.

Michael said no more.

Healiangel knelt before the root. He set his palm against the Veil at a distance no eye could measure. Raphael’s metal band lay cold around his wrist. The two human rhythms remained steady.

He closed his eyes.

First, Earth.

Water moving through soil. Roots holding the bank. Heat sleeping in stone burned during an age long past. Countless small lives crawling beneath the mud, unaware that fire had once fallen from the sky upon this place.

Then, the Veil.

It was not a wall. Each layer preserved a different relationship: light to its source, weight to the place where it fell, sound to direction, memory to the realm that had formed it. The layers were not alive as a being was alive. They contracted, yielded, and found their positions again the way metal returned to the shape in which it had been forged once pressure was removed.

The cut passed through them all.

Healiangel touched the lower edge.

There was no cry.

No memory of pain.

Only a cold, immaculate instruction: this part belonged on the left, that part on the right. The two sides were not permitted to remember each other.

He withdrew his hand.

A gray thread of light clung to his fingertip, fine as ash.

“It did not tear the Veil,” he said. “It made the two edges forget they had once been one.”

Uriel did not alter his stance. “Can the memory be restored?”

“An ordinary wound retains the shape it held before it was harmed. I only help it return.”

“And this line?” Michael asked.

Healiangel looked at the gray trace on his hand. “There is no former shape left to return to.”

Lucifer stepped nearer. “Then we preserve it. Observe it. If whatever made the cut tries again, next time we will see.”

Michael pulled his sword from the ground.

The moment its weight left the riverbank, the line widened to the breadth of a finger.

Sound vanished.

Not only around the tree.

Water, leaves, the breathing of the four angels—all were severed from the places that produced them. Healiangel could feel his throat moving but heard no voice. In the garden, Adam and Lilith turned at once. They could not see the angels, yet the sudden silence drew them close together.

Uriel drove both wings downward.

Four amber pillars rose around the tree. Their light did not close the cut; it established a boundary around the portion of space losing direction. Beyond the pillars, branches continued to move. Within them, leaves stood still inside the wind.

Michael planted the sword again.

The ground groaned. Gravity forced the line to open more slowly, but the silver light along the blade split toward either side.

Lucifer raised both hands.

He did not strike the cut. Light from his wings curled into a vast arch over the space between the river and Eden. Where direction had vanished, his radiance gave every ray a point to return to. The shadows stopped sliding. The current found its banks again. Adam watched the sunlight change color across his hand, never seeing the second sky that kept the world around him from coming apart.

Healiangel heard the call.

This time it did not come from the Veil.

It traveled along the cut, using his own mark to find a way into his being. The vibration spread through his wings and replayed itself in reverse: thousands of connections contracting into a line, the line into a point, the point approaching a state in which nothing remained joined to anything.

His dark-blue wings opened with a violent snap.

Gray-silver spread outward from their roots, not blazing, but laying itself over each tier of feathers like moonlight on old metal.

Michael called his name.

The sound did not reach him.

Healiangel could still read the movement of his lips.

He placed both hands on either side of the cut.

Cold entered his wrists. It did not take memory at once. It searched for a shape complete enough to replace what the Veil had forgotten.

Healiangel possessed such a shape.

The three beats of passage.

The first layer warm as sunlit stone. The second cold enough to draw the light inward within his wing-bones. The third, a silence with a surface, yielding around his being before returning to itself once he had passed. He had recorded that order inside himself the first time he descended to Earth—not as recollection, but as a healer records the placement of every filament before closing a wound.

If he placed that structural memory into the cut, the two edges would have a pattern through which to recognize one another.

He also knew what would be lost.

Not his name.

Not Raphael’s face, Lucifer’s hand, or Michael’s voice.

Not the Lower Realm, the dead who had lain in his hands, or the two humans who had just pulled one another from the river.

Only the structural path that had closed around him in three beats.

A memory-mark.

Something he could live without.

And something that, once given, he would never use in the same way again.

Lucifer stepped between two of the amber pillars.

The light on his wings was torn free of direction and whipped in bands around his shoulders. Still he came forward and seized Healiangel’s wrist.

The words did not travel through air. They passed through touch.

Do not.

Healiangel opened his eyes.

There was no command in Lucifer’s gaze. Only the too-late realization that the question he wanted preserved was demanding that someone else pay its price.

Healiangel turned his hand and placed his fingers around Lucifer’s wrist.

I know what it will take.

You cannot be certain.

I am certain this cannot go farther.

Lucifer looked toward Eden. Adam and Lilith stood hand in hand within the light he held, unaware that the space around them had lost all sound.

We can contain it.

For how long?

Lucifer did not answer.

One amber pillar cracked across its center.

Uriel dropped to one knee. The southern edge of his wing darkened like metal plunged into cold water. Michael locked both hands around the sword hilt. The lines beneath his armor flared, then died from shoulder to elbow.

Healiangel tightened his hold on Lucifer’s wrist one final time.

Release me.

Lucifer did not.

Michael took one hand from the sword and placed it on Lucifer’s shoulder.

They looked at each other through the silence.

Michael did not drag Lucifer away. He merely took the weight Lucifer had forgotten he was pressing into Healiangel’s wrist.

Lucifer’s fingers opened.

Healiangel turned back to the cut.

He gave it the memory-mark.

No radiance exploded.

The first sensation was warmth beneath his feet, the way the first layer of the Veil had once embraced his being. He placed it upon the left edge.

Then came cold contracting through his wing-bones. He placed it upon the right.

Last came the silence with a surface. Healiangel drew it across the space between the two sides.

The cut resisted.

Not with force. It simply continued to preserve its single instruction: the two edges had never belonged together.

Healiangel remembered Adam’s and Lilith’s hands locking above the river.

Two beings had not needed a song written before them to know they could stand together.

He did not force the edges back into their former shape.

He gave them a new moment in which to belong to one another.

His gray-silver wings folded forward.

The three structural beats passed through him, left his being, and entered the Veil.

On the first beat, the cut narrowed.

On the second, sound returned all at once: the river striking its bank, Uriel’s wings trembling within the pillars, Michael’s breath forcing its way between his teeth, Lucifer calling Healiangel’s name—this time through the air.

On the third, the edges met.

The cut closed.

Healiangel fell forward.

Lucifer caught him before his knees struck the ground. Michael’s weight came through both their shoulders and kept them from sliding down the bank. Uriel folded his wings. The four amber pillars shattered into countless fragments of light, falling through the grass before going dark.

In the garden, Adam and Lilith looked up together when the river found its voice again.

Adam spoke her name.

Lilith answered with his.

Then they released each other, each took one end of the trunk, and together they pulled it back toward the water.

✦

Raphael asked Healiangel seven questions.

They had returned to Heaven. The healing chamber nearest the Veil had been sealed, leaving only the white light from channels in the ceiling and the faint amber still clinging to the edges of Uriel’s wings. Healiangel sat on a low stone slab. His wings had returned to deep blue, but several feathers near the roots still flashed silver whenever he breathed.

Raphael stood before him.

“Your name?”

“Healiangel.”

“Who crossed the passage first?”

“Michael.”

“Who crossed last?”

“Uriel.”

“Who held the two life-rhythms?”

Healiangel looked at the metal band now restored to Raphael’s wrist. “You did.”

“What did you see at the river?”

“Adam and Lilith pulling one another from the water.”

“What did Lucifer do when the cut opened?”

“He kept light oriented around Eden.”

Raphael paused before the final question.

“In what order did the three layers of passage close?”

Healiangel opened his mouth.

He remembered crossing.

He remembered Michael going first. Raphael’s hand on his shoulder. The smell of wet earth striking him as Earth’s gravity drew his body down. He still knew that the passage required three beats to close, because he himself had counted them.

But when he searched for the first layer, he found only an edgeless vacancy.

He tried to work backward from the last.

There was no path.

“I do not know.”

Lucifer stood beside the western wall. His hand closed.

Michael faced him from the opposite side, still wearing his armor. Light continued to leak beneath the elbow of his sword arm.

Raphael knelt until he was level with Healiangel’s eyes. “You do not remember crossing?”

“I remember.”

“You do not remember who crossed with you?”

“I remember all of them.”

“Then where is the loss?”

Healiangel looked at his hands. “I know the Veil closed around my being. I no longer know how it did so.”

Raphael placed two fingers between his brows. White light entered very slowly, not searching for a memory to draw back, but tracing the outline of the empty space.

After a time, he withdrew his hand.

“A structural memory-mark,” Raphael said.

At the entrance, Gabriel inscribed those words into the ring of characters around his staff.

Healiangel looked at him. “Will it spread?”

“No.” Raphael answered at once. “Your name, bonds, choices, and lived memories remain intact. What was taken is only the pattern you recorded from the Veil.”

“Can he learn it again?” Michael asked.

Raphael did not answer for him.

Healiangel closed his eyes and tried to feel the layers enclosing the healing chamber. He could still sense the tension of the boundary. Still hear where Heaven’s light met the weight rising from Earth. But whenever he searched for the order that joined them, the perception slipped from his grasp.

“Perhaps,” he said. “But not through the old mark.”

Lucifer left the wall.

“Then it took the one thing that would have allowed him to close it again.”

“It did not take it by itself,” Michael said. “Healiangel chose.”

“Yes.” Lucifer looked at him. “That is always the first thing said by the one standing outside the cost.”

The air in the chamber grew heavy.

Raphael kept one hand on Healiangel’s shoulder. Gabriel stopped inscribing. Uriel remained near the door, silently studying the amber trace still left on his wing.

Michael came forward.

“I held the cut.”

Lucifer gave one short laugh. “You always hold until the moment you have to let go.”

Michael’s gloved hand tightened.

The light beneath his elbow flared, passed through a seam in the armor, and ran toward his wrist. He did not look at it.

“This time I did not let go.”

Lucifer looked at Healiangel sitting beneath Raphael’s hand.

“No,” he said. “This time he held in your place.”

Michael stopped two steps away.

The space between them was no longer a handspan, no longer a passage narrow enough for only one person. It was as wide as the chamber, with room for Raphael, Uriel, Gabriel, and Healiangel to stand inside it and still fail to touch both sides.

Healiangel rose.

His knees wavered. Raphael offered a hand, but Healiangel shook his head and found his balance alone.

“Do not use what I chose to defeat each other.”

Lucifer turned. “I am not—”

“You are.” Healiangel looked at him, then at Michael. “Both of you.”

His voice was not loud. The few silver feathers at the roots of his wings still brightened with each breath, making every sentence seem to come from a place in him that had not fully closed.

“I did not give that memory-mark to Michael’s order,” he said. “Nor did I give it to end Lucifer’s question. I did it because the cut was moving toward two beings who do not yet know the name of fear, and because none of us knows what the next opening might take from them.”

Lucifer looked down at the wrist he had gripped too hard.

Michael removed his hand from the sword.

Healiangel continued. “If you turn that choice into proof that one of you was right, then the cost did not end with me.”

No one answered.

Raphael broke the silence.

“He needs rest.”

Gabriel turned the ring of characters around his staff. “From this moment, every passage through the Veil will require two mark-bearers on each side. No one will touch the site of the cut alone. Every record of the structure we observed will remain under Council seal until we determine whether it can be repeated.”

Lucifer raised his head. “Under seal.”

“So rumor does not turn an unknown line into a door every curious mind longs to open.”

“Or so the Council can decide who is permitted to know that they are threatened?”

“So there will not be a second person paying the same price before we understand it,” Michael said.

Lucifer turned toward him. “You have already decided.”

“I saw it open toward Humanity.”

“You saw a threat. I saw the first sign that something exists beyond what Heaven is willing to name.”

“And you would have kept it open.”

“I would have looked before striking at what I do not understand.”

Michael stepped closer. “If an answer must pass through Healiangel’s being to reach you, it is not yet worthy of being heard.”

This time Lucifer did not answer at once.

Light from the ceiling moved across his face. It found nowhere to settle in his eyes.

“You still decide where my question is allowed to stand,” he said.

“I decide where a question is not permitted to be answered with another person’s being.”

“He is not dead.”

Michael looked at the feathers still silver at the roots of Healiangel’s wings. “Not because we understood what we were doing.”

They stood without moving.

No sword was drawn. No power changed the color of stone. Yet Healiangel heard something shift within the distance between them. Before this, every question Lucifer asked had still been directed at Michael, as though even in defiance he believed Michael might answer. This time, the question passed Michael and continued toward somewhere else.

Michael heard it too.

He was the first to step back.

“Uriel,” Gabriel said. “You will hold the Veil.”

Uriel left the threshold.

“I will hold the position,” he said. “No one can guard an unknown line by pretending it has disappeared.”

Lucifer’s gaze rested on him.

Then he turned and left the healing chamber.

Michael did not call him back.

✦

By the next cycle of light, the place where the cut had been no longer left any visible mark.

The Veil was whole. Light from the golden river passed through its surface, descended to Earth, and returned along the proper course. Sound did not lose its source. Weight no longer slipped from the place where it fell. Gabriel’s seven layers of sealing surrounded the site, each with a narrow opening through which Uriel’s amber light could pass.

Uriel stood alone before the boundary.

At least, he believed he did until he heard Healiangel’s steps on the final stair.

“Raphael told you to rest.”

“He told me not to heal anything else.”

“That is how Raphael says rest.”

Healiangel stopped at the outer seal. “Do you always obey him?”

“When he speaks of wounds.” Uriel looked at the silver still remaining near the roots of Healiangel’s wings. “You have one.”

“An absence.”

“An absence with edges is a wound.”

Healiangel looked at the Veil. “I want to know whether its edges have changed.”

Uriel did not stop him. He shifted aside, opening a narrow amber path between two layers of sealing.

Healiangel entered.

He placed his hand where the cut had been. The surface was warm and taut. The marks of Michael, Lucifer, and Uriel had been completely withdrawn. Raphael’s remained only on Heaven’s side. He searched for his own.

There was none.

It should have reassured him.

Instead, the empty place in his memory trembled.

“Do you still remember closing it?” Uriel asked.

“Yes.”

“Do you remember why?”

“Yes.”

“Do you remember how?”

Healiangel shook his head.

Uriel lowered one wing. A strand of amber light touched the place beneath Healiangel’s hand, divided into three segments, then joined again.

“I recorded the structure you used,” he said. “Not enough to repeat it. Enough to recognize it.”

Healiangel studied the three segments.

He knew they belonged to him the way one knows a scar lies upon the body even after the blade that made it can no longer be felt. But none of the segments opened a path back to the missing memory.

“If it appears again,” he said, “I may not be able to close it.”

“That is why, next time, it will not be only you.”

“You sound like Michael.”

“Michael says many are needed to pass judgment.” Uriel withdrew the strand of light. “I say many are needed so one person does not have to become the entire structure.”

Healiangel looked at him.

Along Uriel’s southern wing, one tier of feathers remained darkened where the amber pillar had broken on Earth. He had not healed it.

“Did you know the price?” Healiangel asked.

“No.”

“Then why did you let me do it?”

Uriel met his gaze. “Because, in that moment, you were the only one who knew where you were placing your hands.”

The answer did not lessen what had happened. Nor did it take the choice away from him.

Healiangel turned back to the Veil.

From above came the golden river, its sound descending through each layer. Beyond it lay Earth’s rhythm, heavy and slow. Deeper still, the two life-currents of Adam and Lilith had returned to rest. Everything occupied its proper place.

Then one segment of amber light on Uriel’s wing went dark.

Both of them looked east.

Not toward the site of the former cut.

Beyond the seven layers of sealing, many rings of towers away, a fine line of light had just crossed the Veil. It did not open the surface. It merely traced three short segments upon it.

The first was warm.

The second was cold.

The last carried no sound.

Healiangel did not recognize the order.

The absence within him did.

For the first time, it hurt.

Uriel spread his wings. Amber light raced eastward, but the three segments vanished before it reached them.

No mark remained upon the Veil.

Only the silence that had returned, shaped exactly like the thing Healiangel had given away.

The cut was no longer calling.

It was answering.

Không phải Địa Giới, những người đã chết trong tay anh, hay hai con người vừa kéo nhau khỏi dòng nước.

Chỉ là con đường cấu trúc đã khép quanh anh trong ba nhịp.

Một dấu nhớ.

Một thứ anh có thể sống mà không có.

Và một thứ, nếu trao đi, anh sẽ không thể dùng lại theo cùng cách.

Lucifer bước vào giữa hai cột hổ phách.

Ánh sáng trên cánh y bị xé khỏi phương hướng, quất thành nhiều dải quanh vai. Y vẫn tiến đến, nắm cổ tay Healiangel.

Tiếng nói không truyền qua không khí. Nó đi bằng tiếp xúc.

Đừng.

Healiangel mở mắt.

Trong mắt Lucifer không có mệnh lệnh. Chỉ có sự nhận ra quá muộn rằng câu hỏi y muốn giữ lại đang đòi một người khác trả giá.

Healiangel xoay bàn tay, đặt các ngón lên cổ tay y.

Ta biết nó lấy gì.

Ngươi không thể chắc.

Ta chắc điều này không được đi xa hơn.

Lucifer nhìn về Eden. Adam và Lilith đang nắm tay nhau giữa vùng sáng y giữ, không biết khoảng không quanh họ đã mất tiếng.

Chúng ta có thể giữ nó.

Đến khi nào?

Lucifer không trả lời.

Một cột hổ phách nứt ngang.

Uriel khuỵu một gối. Mép cánh phía nam của ngài sẫm lại như kim loại bị nhúng vào nước lạnh. Michael ghì cả hai tay lên chuôi kiếm. Những đường sáng dưới giáp chàng bùng rồi tắt dần từ vai xuống khuỷu.

Healiangel siết cổ tay Lucifer lần cuối.

Buông ta ra.

Lucifer không buông.

Michael rời một tay khỏi kiếm và đặt lên vai y.

Hai người nhìn nhau qua sự im lặng.

Michael không kéo Lucifer lại. Chàng chỉ giữ phần trọng lượng mà y đã quên mình đang dồn lên cổ tay Healiangel.

Các ngón tay Lucifer mở ra.

Healiangel quay về vết cắt.

Anh đưa dấu nhớ vào đó.

Không có ánh sáng bùng nổ.

Cảm giác đầu tiên là hơi ấm dưới lòng bàn chân, như lớp đầu của Tấm Màn đã từng ôm lấy bản thể anh. Anh đặt nó lên mép trái.

Sau đó là cái lạnh co trong xương cánh. Anh đặt nó lên mép phải.

Cuối cùng là lớp im có bề mặt. Healiangel kéo nó qua khoảng không giữa hai phía.

Đường cắt chống lại.

Không bằng sức mạnh. Nó chỉ tiếp tục giữ một mệnh lệnh duy nhất: hai mép không từng thuộc về nhau.

Healiangel nhớ bàn tay Adam và Lilith siết lại trên bờ sông.

Hai sinh thể không cần một bài ca có trước để biết mình có thể cùng đứng.

Anh không ép hai mép trở lại hình dạng cũ.

Anh cho chúng một lần thuộc về nhau mới.

Đôi cánh bạc xám khép về phía trước.

Ba nhịp cấu trúc đi qua anh, rời khỏi bản thể và đặt vào Tấm Màn.

Ở nhịp đầu, đường cắt hẹp lại.

Ở nhịp thứ hai, âm thanh trở về cùng lúc. Tiếng sông đập vào bờ. Tiếng cánh Uriel rung trong cột sáng. Tiếng Michael thở bật qua kẽ răng. Tiếng Lucifer gọi Healiangel, lần này truyền được qua không khí.

Ở nhịp thứ ba, hai mép chạm nhau.

Vết cắt khép.

Healiangel ngã về phía trước.

Lucifer đỡ lấy anh trước khi đầu gối chạm đất. Sức nặng từ Michael dồn qua vai cả hai, giữ họ không trượt xuống bờ sông. Uriel gập cánh. Bốn cột hổ phách vỡ thành vô số mảnh sáng, rơi qua cỏ rồi tắt.

Trong khu vườn, Adam và Lilith cùng ngẩng lên khi tiếng nước trở lại.

Adam nói tên nàng.

Lilith đáp tên chàng.

Rồi họ buông tay, mỗi người nhặt một đầu thân cây và cùng kéo nó về phía dòng nước.

✦

Raphael hỏi Healiangel bảy câu.

Họ đã trở lại Thiên Đàng. Gian chữa lành gần Tấm Màn được đóng kín, chỉ còn ánh sáng trắng từ những rãnh trên trần và quầng hổ phách rất nhạt bám ở mép cánh Uriel. Healiangel ngồi trên một phiến đá thấp. Đôi cánh đã trở về màu xanh sẫm, nhưng vài sợi lông gần gốc còn ánh bạc mỗi khi anh thở.

Raphael đứng trước mặt anh.

“Tên ngươi?”

“Healiangel.”

“Người đầu tiên đi qua lối mở?”

“Michael.”

“Người cuối cùng?”

“Uriel.”

“Ai giữ hai nhịp sống?”

Healiangel nhìn dải kim loại đã trở lại cổ tay Raphael. “Ngài.”

“Ngươi thấy gì ở bờ sông?”

“Adam và Lilith kéo nhau khỏi nước.”

“Lucifer đã làm gì khi đường cắt mở?”

“Giữ ánh sáng có phương hướng quanh Eden.”

Raphael dừng trước câu cuối.

“Ba lớp của lối đi khép theo thứ tự nào?”

Healiangel mở miệng.

Anh nhớ mình đã bước qua.

Nhớ Michael đi trước. Nhớ bàn tay Raphael trên vai. Nhớ mùi đất ẩm ập vào khi trọng lực Trái Đất kéo cơ thể xuống. Anh còn biết lối mở cần ba nhịp để khép, vì chính mình từng đếm chúng.

Nhưng khi tìm lớp đầu tiên, anh chỉ gặp một khoảng trống không có cạnh.

Anh thử đi từ lớp cuối trở lại.

Không có đường.

“Ta không biết.”

Lucifer đứng cạnh bức tường phía tây. Bàn tay y khép lại.

Michael ở phía đối diện, giáp chưa được tháo. Một đường sáng vẫn rịn dưới khuỷu tay cầm kiếm.

Raphael quỳ xuống ngang tầm mắt Healiangel. “Ngươi không nhớ đã đi qua sao?”

“Ta nhớ.”

“Không nhớ ai đi cùng?”

“Ta nhớ tất cả.”

“Vậy phần mất nằm ở đâu?”

Healiangel nhìn bàn tay mình. “Ta biết Tấm Màn đã khép quanh bản thể ta. Ta không còn biết nó làm bằng cách nào.”

Raphael đặt hai ngón lên giữa trán anh. Ánh sáng trắng đi vào rất chậm, không tìm ký ức để kéo về mà chỉ lần theo đường viền của khoảng trống.

Một lúc sau, ngài rút tay.

“Dấu nhớ cấu trúc,” Raphael nói.

Gabriel đang đứng bên lối vào khắc lại bốn chữ ấy vào vòng ký tự trên trượng.

Healiangel nhìn ngài. “Nó có lan không?”

“Không.” Raphael đáp ngay. “Tên, quan hệ, lựa chọn và ký ức đời sống của ngươi còn nguyên. Phần bị lấy chỉ là mô hình ngươi đã ghi từ Tấm Màn.”

“Có thể học lại?” Michael hỏi.

Raphael không trả lời thay anh.

Healiangel nhắm mắt, thử chạm vào những lớp đang bao quanh cả gian chữa lành. Anh vẫn cảm thấy độ căng của ranh giới. Vẫn nghe được nơi ánh sáng Thiên Đàng chạm vào sức nặng từ Trái Đất. Nhưng hễ tìm thứ tự đưa chúng về với nhau, cảm nhận lại trượt khỏi tay.

“Có thể,” anh nói. “Nhưng không bằng dấu cũ.”

Lucifer rời tường.

“Vậy nó đã lấy thứ duy nhất giúp anh ấy khép nó lần nữa.”

“Nó không tự lấy,” Michael nói. “Healiangel đã chọn.”

“Phải.” Lucifer nhìn chàng. “Đó luôn là lời người đứng ngoài cái giá nói trước tiên.”

Không khí trong gian chữa lành nặng xuống.

Raphael vẫn đặt một tay trên vai Healiangel. Gabriel ngừng khắc. Uriel đứng bên cửa, im lặng nhìn đường sáng hổ phách còn sót trên cánh mình.

Michael bước đến.

“Ta đã giữ đường cắt.”

Lucifer bật cười, chỉ một tiếng. “Ngươi luôn giữ cho đến lúc phải buông.”

Bàn tay mang găng của Michael khép lại.

Đường sáng dưới khuỷu tay chàng bùng lên, xuyên qua một khe giáp rồi chảy xuống cổ tay. Chàng không nhìn nó.

“Lần này ta không buông.”

Lucifer nhìn Healiangel đang ngồi dưới tay Raphael.

“Không,” y nói. “Lần này anh ấy giữ thay ngươi.”

Michael dừng cách y hai bước.

Khoảng trống giữa họ không còn là một gang tay, không còn là một lối đi chỉ đủ cho một người bước qua. Nó rộng bằng căn phòng, đủ chỗ cho Raphael, Uriel, Gabriel và Healiangel đứng bên trong mà vẫn không chạm được hai phía.

Healiangel đứng lên.

Đầu gối anh chao nhẹ. Raphael đưa tay, nhưng anh lắc đầu và tự giữ thăng bằng.

“Đừng dùng điều ta chọn để thắng nhau.”

Lucifer quay lại. “Ta không—”

“Có.” Healiangel nhìn y, rồi nhìn Michael. “Cả hai ngươi.”

Giọng anh không lớn. Vài sợi lông bạc ở gốc cánh vẫn sáng theo từng hơi thở, khiến mỗi câu như đi ra từ một nơi trong anh chưa khép hoàn toàn.

“Ta không trả dấu nhớ ấy cho trật tự của Michael,” anh nói. “Cũng không trả nó để đóng câu hỏi của Lucifer. Ta làm vì đường cắt đang đi về phía hai sinh thể chưa biết tên của sợ hãi, và vì không ai trong chúng ta biết lần mở kế tiếp sẽ lấy khỏi họ điều gì.”

Lucifer nhìn xuống cổ tay mình, nơi anh đã nắm Healiangel quá chặt.

Michael tháo bàn tay khỏi chuôi kiếm.

Healiangel tiếp tục: “Nếu các ngươi biến lựa chọn đó thành bằng chứng rằng một người đúng, vậy cái giá chưa dừng ở ta.”

Không ai đáp.

Raphael là người phá quãng lặng.

“Anh ấy cần nghỉ.”

Gabriel quay vòng ký tự trên trượng. “Từ giờ, mọi lối đi qua Tấm Màn phải có hai người giữ dấu ở mỗi phía. Không ai chạm vào vị trí vết cắt một mình. Tất cả ghi nhận về cấu trúc vừa thấy sẽ được đặt dưới niêm phong của Hội đồng cho đến khi xác định nó có thể bị lặp lại hay không.”

Lucifer ngẩng lên. “Đặt dưới niêm phong.”

“Để lời đồn không biến một đường chưa biết thành cánh cửa mà bất kỳ kẻ tò mò nào cũng muốn mở.”

“Hay để Hội đồng quyết định ai được biết mình đang bị đe dọa?”

“Để không có người thứ hai phải trả cùng một giá trước khi chúng ta hiểu giá ấy.” Michael nói.

Lucifer quay về phía chàng. “Ngươi đã quyết định rồi.”

“Ta đã thấy nó mở về phía Nhân Loại.”

“Ngươi thấy một nguy cơ. Ta thấy dấu đầu tiên cho biết có điều tồn tại ngoài những gì Thiên Đàng chịu gọi tên.”

“Và ngươi sẵn sàng giữ nó mở.”

“Ta sẵn sàng nhìn trước khi chém vào thứ ta không hiểu.”

Michael bước sát hơn. “Nếu câu trả lời phải đi qua bản thể Healiangel để đến với ngươi, nó chưa xứng đáng được nghe.”

Lần này Lucifer không đáp ngay.

Ánh sáng từ trần chạy dọc gương mặt y. Nó không tìm được chỗ dừng trong mắt.

“Ngươi vẫn quyết định câu hỏi của ta được phép đứng ở đâu,” y nói.

“Ta quyết định nơi một câu hỏi không được trả bằng bản thể của người khác.”

“Anh ấy chưa chết.”

Michael nhìn những sợi lông còn bạc ở gốc cánh Healiangel. “Không phải vì chúng ta biết mình đang làm gì.”

Hai người đứng yên.

Không kiếm nào được rút. Không quyền năng nào làm đá đổi màu. Nhưng Healiangel nghe một điều trong khoảng trống giữa họ đã chuyển vị trí. Trước đây, mỗi câu hỏi của Lucifer vẫn hướng về Michael, như thể dù chống lại, y vẫn tin chàng là người có thể trả lời. Lần này, câu hỏi đi ngang qua Michael và tiếp tục đến một nơi khác.

Michael cũng nghe thấy.

Chàng là người lùi trước.

“Uriel,” Gabriel gọi. “Ngươi giữ Tấm Màn.”

Uriel rời khỏi ngưỡng cửa.

“Ta sẽ giữ vị trí,” ngài nói. “Không ai giữ được một đường chưa biết bằng cách giả vờ nó đã biến mất.”

Ánh mắt Lucifer dừng ở ngài.

Rồi y quay lưng, đi khỏi gian chữa lành.

Michael không gọi lại.

Đến vòng sáng kế tiếp, vị trí vết cắt không còn để lại dấu bằng mắt.

Tấm Màn đã liền. Ánh sáng từ dòng sông vàng đi qua bề mặt, xuống Trái Đất rồi trở về theo đúng hướng. Âm thanh không bị mất. Trọng lượng không trượt khỏi nơi nó rơi. Bảy lớp niêm phong của Gabriel bao quanh khu vực, mỗi lớp có một đoạn mở dành cho ánh hổ phách của Uriel đi qua.

Uriel đứng một mình trước ranh giới.

Ít nhất ngài nghĩ vậy cho đến khi nghe bước chân Healiangel trên bậc cuối.

“Raphael bảo ngươi nghỉ.”

“Ngài ấy bảo ta không chữa thêm.”

“Đó là cách Raphael nói nghỉ.”

Healiangel dừng bên vòng niêm phong ngoài. “Ngươi luôn nghe lời ngài ấy sao?”

“Khi ngài ấy nói về vết thương.” Uriel nhìn vài sợi bạc còn ở gốc cánh anh. “Ngươi có một cái.”

“Một khoảng trống.”

“Khoảng trống có bờ là vết thương.”

Healiangel nhìn Tấm Màn. “Ta muốn biết bờ của nó có đổi không.”

Uriel không ngăn. Ngài dịch sang một bên, để ánh hổ phách mở thành một lối hẹp giữa hai lớp niêm phong.

Healiangel bước vào.

Anh đặt tay lên nơi đường cắt từng nằm. Bề mặt ấm và căng. Dấu của Michael, Lucifer, Uriel đã được rút sạch. Dấu của Raphael chỉ còn ở phía Thiên Đàng. Anh tìm dấu của mình.

Không có.

Điều đó đáng lẽ phải khiến anh yên tâm.

Thay vào đó, khoảng trống trong trí nhớ rung lên.

“Ngươi còn nhớ đã khép nó không?” Uriel hỏi.

“Có.”

“Nhớ vì sao?”

“Có.”

“Nhớ bằng cách nào?”

Healiangel lắc đầu.

Uriel hạ một cánh. Một sợi sáng hổ phách chạm vào vị trí bàn tay anh, tách thành ba đoạn rồi nối lại.

“Ta đã ghi cấu trúc ngươi dùng,” ngài nói. “Không đủ để lặp. Đủ để nhận ra.”

Healiangel nhìn ba đoạn sáng.

Anh biết chúng thuộc về mình theo cách người ta biết một vết sẹo nằm trên cơ thể dù không còn cảm thấy lưỡi kiếm đã tạo ra nó. Nhưng không đoạn nào mở được con đường trở lại phần ký ức đã mất.

“Nếu nó xuất hiện lần nữa,” anh nói, “ta có thể không khép được.”

“Vì vậy lần sau không chỉ có ngươi.”

“Ngươi nói như Michael.”

“Michael nói cần nhiều người để phán quyết.” Uriel thu sợi sáng. “Ta nói cần nhiều người để một kẻ không phải trở thành toàn bộ cấu trúc.”

Healiangel nhìn ngài.

Trên cánh Uriel, một lớp lông ở mép phía nam vẫn sẫm màu do cột sáng đã vỡ dưới Trái Đất. Ngài chưa chữa nó.

“Ngươi đã biết cái giá sao?” Healiangel hỏi.

“Không.”

“Vậy vì sao ngươi để ta làm?”

Uriel nhìn thẳng vào anh. “Vì lúc ấy ngươi là người duy nhất biết mình đang đặt tay vào đâu.”

Câu trả lời không làm nhẹ đi điều đã xảy ra. Nó cũng không lấy lựa chọn khỏi anh.

Healiangel quay về Tấm Màn.

Từ phía trên, tiếng sông vàng đi xuống từng lớp. Xa hơn là nhịp Trái Đất, nặng và chậm. Bên dưới nữa, hai mạch sống của Adam và Lilith đã trở về trạng thái nghỉ. Mọi thứ ở đúng vị trí.

Rồi ánh hổ phách trên cánh Uriel tắt một đoạn.

Cả hai cùng nhìn sang phía đông.

Không phải vị trí vết cắt cũ.

Ở ngoài bảy lớp niêm phong, cách họ nhiều vòng tháp, một đường sáng mảnh vừa chạy qua Tấm Màn. Nó không mở bề mặt. Chỉ vạch lên đó ba đoạn ngắn.

Đoạn thứ nhất ấm.

Đoạn thứ hai lạnh.

Đoạn cuối không mang âm thanh.

Healiangel không nhận ra thứ tự ấy.

Khoảng trống trong anh nhận ra.

Nó đau lần đầu tiên.

Uriel mở cánh. Ánh hổ phách lao về phía đông, nhưng ba đoạn sáng đã tắt trước khi chạm tới.

Trên Tấm Màn không còn dấu nào.

Chỉ có phần im lặng vừa trở về, mang đúng hình dạng của thứ Healiangel đã trao đi.

Vết cắt không còn gọi. Nó đang trả lời.

— HẾT CHƯƠNG 4 —
